analysis: The only change in .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml is to comments: head lines 56-58 for build-cluster and head lines 862-864 for cluster-release-checks. They now say that when job sizes are off, the lanes ask without a size and get the approval's pinned macOS size. Previously they said the jobs ran on Blacksmith. No steps, runner expressions, permissions, secrets, cache keys or action pins change, so there is no behavioral diff. The workflow keeps top-level `permissions: contents: read`, `persist-credentials: false` on checkouts, and SHA-pinned actions. No provider code, coordinator protocol, attestation, App Attest, key custody or prefix-cache code is touched. T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-011 are not affected. The CI cache and runner-routing text is outside the provider threat model's scope. The comments describe runner routing in provider-plan.yml, which is not in the supplied evidence. That is an unverified external contract, so I report no finding. In the workflow, `runs-on` still comes from `fromJSON(inputs.routes)`, which is populated by the caller workflows and provider-plan.yml. Those files were not supplied, so I could not check how the pinned-size fallback is chosen. That choice is a CI runner-selection matter, not a runtime security regression.
